page3_s1.raw_text: New York State law requires an insurer issuing or delivering a policy that satisfies the requirements of New York Vehicle and Traffic Law article 6 to provide supplemental spousal liability insurance upon payment of the premium if the policy is a non-commercial motor vehicle policy and a first named insured has indicated that such insured has a spouse on the insurance application or if supplemental spousal liability insurance is currently on the policy, unless a first named insured elects, in writing, to decline and refuse such insurance in the policy.

page3_s2.raw_text: Supplemental spousal liability insurance provides bodily injury liability coverage under a motor vehicle insurance policy when a person is injured or killed in a motor vehicle accident caused by the negligence of the person’s spouse.

page3_s3.raw_text: This coverage is included within the policy’s bodily injury liability limits and does not increase the amount of those limits. For example:

page3_s4.raw_text: Insured’s bodily injury policy coverage limit available to all other claimants subject to a maximum of $100,000 per person: $225,000

page3_s5.raw_text: This example assumes the spouse and other claimants involved in the accident have a right to sue the insured for economic loss or for non-economic loss (i.e., pain and suffering) sustained as a result of a “serious injury” as defined in Insurance Law section 5102(d). It must also have been shown that there was negligence on the part of the insured.

page9_s1.raw_text: Supplemental Spousal Liability covers bodily injury to an insured's spouse under Coverage A (bodily injury) where an insured spouse becomes liable because of the death of or injury to their spouse, even where the injured spouse must prove the culpable conduct of the insured spouse. This applies only to motor vehicle liability insurance policies that satisfy the requirements of Article 6 of the New York Vehicle and Traffic law. This coverage is provided to a first named insured who has indicated they have a spouse on the application. This coverage is included in all policies where the first named insured has indicated they have a spouse on the application unless the first named insured has chosen to exclude this coverage in writing which is indicated in the Coverages, Limits of Liability and Premiums section of the Declarations Page. This coverage is also available if requested in writing by an insured.

page11_s1.raw_text: This Notice provides information regarding shared vehicle arrangements through a Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing Program and the potential insurance implications for the shared vehicle owner.

page11_s2.raw_text: Your Travelers policy will not provide coverage for “Your covered auto” while the motor vehicle is being used through a peer-to-peer car sharing program during the peer-to-peer car sharing period. In addition, Travelers does not offer Peer-to-Peer Car Sharing coverage on an optional basis.

page11_s3.raw_text: For purposes of this Notice, the following terms are defined below:

page11_s4.raw_text: 1. “Peer-to-peer car sharing” shall mean the authorized use of a shared vehicle by an individual other than the vehicle’s owner through a peer-to-peer car sharing program. 2. “Peer-to-peer car sharing program” or “program” means a program that facilitates the use or operation of a shared vehicle by a shared vehicle driver. 3. All other definitions related to peer-to-peer car sharing can be found in Section 900 of Article 40 of the General Business Law.

page12_s1.raw_text: The Rental Vehicle Coverage endorsement to this policy provides protection in the event of damage to, or loss of, a rental vehicle, including loss of use, as described in the endorsement.

page12_s2.raw_text: Rental Vehicle Coverage is mandated by New York State law to reduce problems that confront consumers and leave them vulnerable to major unanticipated costs when dealing with rental vehicle companies.

page12_s3.raw_text: This Rental Vehicle Coverage protects you whenever rental vehicles are rented and operated any where within the United States, its territories or possessions, and Canada.

page12_s4.raw_text: Rental Vehicle Coverage is not applicable while the motor vehicle is used through a peer-to-peer car sharing program pursuant to article 40 of the General Business Law.

page12_s5.raw_text: In the event that a premium is at any time charged or increased for Rental Vehicle Coverage, you have the right to reject this coverage and not pay such charge, if you so inform your insurer within ten calendar days after you receive notice that such a premium charge or increase will be made for Rental Vehicle Coverage.
